To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Ust and 2-O sulfate groups on the low affinity receptor CS/DS are involved in cell motility and cell adhesion of B-16 mouse melanoma cells, and that Ust and the 2-O sulfate group on CS/DS are required for the formation of pulmonary metastasis of the B-16 mouse model.
UST and UST-dependent sulfation of CS/DS are important regulators of cell adhesion and migration.
Ust and consequently 2-0 sulfation of CS/DS reduces Itga5, which leads to an impaired cell adhesion and migration in mouse and human melanoma cells.

the identification of novel therapeutic targets for metastatic melanoma.
the role of UST and 2-O sulfate groups on cell migration and adhesion in melanoma.
the elucidation of the role of Ust in metastasis and the potential of Ust as a novel target for the treatment of malignant melanoma.
